tasks.prompt:
Lumen needs a command palette. Inside a shared app layout with three screens (a dashboard at `/`, projects at `/projects`, members at `/members`), pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) opens a palette with a search field. Results are grouped under "Pages" (the three screens), "Actions" ("Create project", "Invite member", "Toggle theme") and "Recent" (three recently opened projects). Typing filters every group; arrow keys move the highlight and Enter runs it. "Invite member" opens a dialog with an email field. A visible button in the header (with the shortcut shown next to it) opens the palette too, so it works on phones.

tasks.prompt:
Lumen's analytics overview at `/` and a signups report at `/reports/signups`, in a shared layout. The overview has four KPI cards (visitors, signups, conversion rate, MRR), each with its change against the previous period, a line chart of daily visitors and signups, a bar chart of signups by channel, and a table of channels sortable by clicking its column headers. A date-range control ("Last 7 days", "Last 14 days", "Last 30 days") and a segment filter ("All users", "New users", "Returning users") sit above the charts, and changing either updates the KPIs and charts (derive the numbers from the data given). The signups report shows a larger signups chart and a daily table, with a link back to the overview.

tasks.prompt:
Lumen's team page. At `/`, a members table shows each person's avatar or initials, name, email, role and status, with role and status as badges. A search field and a role filter narrow the table. Each row has an actions menu ("Change role", "Resend invite" for invited people, "Remove"). An "Invite member" button opens a dialog with a form: email (required, must be valid), role (required) and an optional message; submitting shows inline errors when the fields are invalid. Each member links to a detail page at `/members/[id]` showing their profile, role, status, join date and recent activity; `/members/m-02` is Daniel Reyes.

tasks.prompt:
Lumen's issue tracker as a list-detail view. At `/` the list shows each issue's id, title, status, priority and assignee, with filters for status and assignee and an empty state when the filters match nothing. Selecting an issue opens it at `/issues/[id]`: on desktop the list stays on the left and the detail fills the right pane; on phones the detail replaces the list and has a back button. The detail shows the title, description, and selects for status and assignee that change the issue, plus an activity timeline. `/issues/LUM-104` is "Checkout fails on Safari 17".
